title: What if the sun never set again?
formula: Strange act (3 AM, blazing sun, you dig a hole) -> why (the sun stopped 40 days ago) -> rival's perfect version (Kyle's pool party that never ends) + mocker ('Who needs night?') -> first fallout (no dark = no sleep: mom's six breakfasts, owls on strike) -> the real threat (no night = no cooling: the stove never turns off; soft roads, egg on the car) -> weird prep, mystery kept (tinfoil baked-potato house, mattress dragged out, thermometer on a string into the hole) -> mocker laughs off his flamingo (plants the flamingo) -> setback (day 40: every AC at once, the grid pops, 120 on the porch, the pool turns to soup) -> tension stretch (five feet, ten, fifteen) -> payoff (dark, quiet, sixty degrees) + 'You see' picnic-cooler analogy -> hidden plan (you checked that string every day: sixty, every time) -> reversal (the lid doesn't fit, a sliver of sun) -> doubter flips ('Mole man... got room?') -> his own toy saves you (the flamingo plugs the gap) -> loop: 'It's 3 AM. And finally... it feels like it.'
loop: Line 1: 'It's 3 AM, the sun is blazing, and you're digging a hole.' Last: 'It's 3 AM. And finally... it feels like it.' (the phone clock reads 3:00 AM in both, blazing sun first, darkness last).

voiceNotes.kyle: Liam (ElevenLabs premade): energetic young man, a loud party-bro neighbour who later begs

facts: Scenario premise: the sun just stops in the sky (never explained; a real stop of Earth's spin would be far worse, so the script does not claim a cause).
Melatonin, the hormone that makes you sleepy, is released by the pineal gland in darkness; light suppresses it (NIH / Sleep Foundation).
At night Earth's surface loses heat by radiating infrared to space; without nights the daily cooling disappears and heat keeps building (basic radiative balance; why deserts cool fast at night).

A few feet underground the soil barely feels daily swings; about 10-20 ft down it sits near the local yearly average, roughly 50-60 F over much of the US (the basis of geothermal heat pumps and root cellars). Heat takes weeks to months to soak down.
Heat waves send air-conditioning demand past what grids can supply, causing blackouts (e.g. California rolling blackouts, August 2020).
Asphalt softens in extreme heat; people in midnight-sun places (Alaska, northern Norway) cover windows with tinfoil or blackout blinds to sleep.
Comic exaggeration: 120 F on the porch after 40 days, owls on strike, the pool turning to soup, six breakfasts a day, the egg on the car, the flamingo plug.

lines.narration: It's 3 AM, the sun is *blazing*, and you're digging a hole in your backyard.
lines.spoken: It's three A.M., the sun is BLAZING, and you're digging a hole in your backyard.
lines.scene: Cold open, a suburban backyard under a hard white noon sun: you, sweaty, in the rust hoodie, shovel deep in a hole, dirt flying; your phone propped on the fence post glows 3:00 AM. Cut on 'blazing' to the sun itself, huge and glaring over the rooftops, heat shimmer.
lines.camera: MCU on you digging, the phone sharp in the foreground; hard cut up to the sun on 'blazing', back down to the hole
lines.gag: The phone says 3:00 AM while the sun blasts like noon

lines.narration: Because 40 days ago, the sun stopped in the sky... and never *set* again.
lines.spoken: Because forty days ago, the sun stopped in the sky... and never set again.
lines.scene: The sun sliding down toward the horizon over the town, then halting dead with a jolt, a little bounce; below it the street's shadows freeze. Insert: a kitchen calendar with 40 days crossed out in red marker.
lines.camera: Wide on the sky, the sun's slide, a snap shake on the stop; hard cut to the calendar push-in
lines.gag: The sun brakes like a car, and bounces

lines.narration: At first, everybody *loves* it.
lines.scene: Your street in full sun: kids on bikes, a sprinkler, an ice cream truck, a grandpa in a deck chair with his shirt off.
lines.camera: Fast tracking move along the street
lines.gag: Grandpa sunbathing in a deck chair, shirt off, arms up

lines.narration: Your neighbor Kyle starts a pool party that *never ends*.
lines.scene: Over the fence: Kyle's backyard pool, Kyle in shades and a tank top lounging on a giant pink inflatable flamingo, a banner over the pool 'ENDLESS SUMMER', speaker booming, a dozen guests.
lines.camera: Crane up over the fence to reveal the party
lines.gag: Kyle on a flamingo the size of a car

lines.narration: "Hey, mole man! Who needs *night*?"
lines.speaker: kyle
lines.scene: Kyle on his flamingo, pointing at you over the fence with his drink, laughing; the guests laugh too.
lines.camera: Telephoto MCU of Kyle, guests laughing behind
lines.gag: The whole party laughs at you in sync

lines.narration: But your brain only makes its sleepy chemical in the *dark*.
lines.scene: Full-frame x-ray insert of your head: a little tap inside your brain dripping blue sleepy drops; a beam of sunlight hits it and the tap screws shut.
lines.camera: Hard cut to the insert, push-in on the tap
lines.gag: Sunlight slams the brain's sleep tap shut

lines.narration: So nobody *sleeps*. Your mom eats breakfast six times a day. And the owls go on *strike*.
lines.spoken: So nobody sleeps. Your mom eats breakfast SIX times a day. And the owls go on strike.
lines.scene: Three beats: you in bed, wide awake, eyes red, tinfoil not yet up, sun blasting through the blinds; your mom at the kitchen table with a stack of six cereal bowls; three owls on the fence holding a little picket sign 'WE WORK NIGHTS'.
lines.camera: Hard cuts, one per beat, the owls get a slow push-in
lines.gag: Owls on a picket line

lines.narration: Then it gets *hot*.
lines.scene: The porch thermometer, needle creeping up; the lawn going yellow.
lines.camera: Macro on the thermometer, the needle moves on 'hot'
lines.gag: The thermometer needle twitches up

lines.narration: Every night, Earth used to cool off, like a pan pulled off the *stove*.
lines.scene: Mini-set: a kitchen stove, a hot frying pan lifted off the glowing burner, steam fading as it cools; the pan's bottom is a little painted Earth.
lines.camera: Insert, the pan lifts off on 'stove'
lines.gag: The pan is a tiny Earth

lines.narration: Now the stove never turns *off*.
lines.spoken: Now the stove NEVER turns off.
lines.scene: The same burner glowing brighter, the knob snaps to MAX by itself and breaks off in a hand; match cut to the sun over your street.
lines.camera: Macro on the knob, match cut to the sun
lines.gag: The knob breaks off in your hand

lines.narration: The road goes soft like *gum*. Kyle fries an egg on his *car*.
lines.scene: A sneaker peeling up from the asphalt with a long sticky string; Kyle cracking an egg on the hood of his car, it sizzles instantly.
lines.camera: Low macro on the sneaker, then MCU on the egg hitting the hood
lines.gag: The road stretches like gum under a shoe

lines.narration: So you get weird. You cover every window in tinfoil, until your house looks like a giant baked *potato*.
lines.scene: You on a ladder taping tinfoil over the last window; pull back to the whole house wrapped in shining foil, glaring in the sun.
lines.camera: MS on you taping, fast pull-out to the whole foil house on 'potato'
lines.gag: Your house is a baked potato

lines.narration: You drag your mattress across the yard, and lower a thermometer into the hole on a *string*.
lines.scene: You hauling your mattress across the lawn, leaning into it; then crouched at the hole, lowering a little thermometer on a string into the dark.
lines.camera: Tracking side-on with the mattress drag, then top-down down the hole as the thermometer sinks
lines.gag: The thermometer disappears into the dark

lines.narration: Kyle laughs so hard, he falls off his *flamingo*.
lines.scene: Kyle cracking up at you, rocking, sliding off the flamingo into the pool, splash.
lines.camera: MS of Kyle, the splash on 'flamingo'
lines.gag: Kyle slides off the flamingo into the pool

lines.narration: Then, on day 40, every air conditioner in town turns on at *once*.
lines.spoken: Then, on day forty, every air conditioner in town turns on at ONCE.
lines.scene: A row of AC units on every house roaring on together, fans spinning, power lines humming and sagging.
lines.camera: Fast whip along the row of AC units
lines.gag: Every AC on the street starts in the same frame

lines.narration: And the power grid goes *pop*.
lines.scene: The transformer on the pole sparks and bangs; every AC whines down and dies, the ice cream truck's music slows to a stop.
lines.camera: MCU on the transformer, a kick on 'pop'
lines.gag: The ice cream truck's tune dies mid-note

lines.narration: The porch thermometer hits 120. Kyle's pool turns into a hot *tub*. Then into *soup*.
lines.spoken: The porch thermometer hits one hundred and twenty. Kyle's pool turns into a hot tub. Then into soup.
lines.scene: The thermometer needle slamming to 120; Kyle's pool steaming, the party guests climbing out red as lobsters; then a floating lettuce leaf and a carrot in the steaming pool, the flamingo deflating sadly.
lines.camera: Macro on the needle, then a wide over the steaming pool, push-in on the carrot
lines.gag: Vegetables floating in Kyle's pool, the flamingo sagging

lines.narration: So you climb down. Five feet. Ten feet. *Fifteen*.
lines.spoken: So you climb down. Five feet. Ten feet. FIFTEEN.
lines.scene: You climbing down a wooden ladder into the hole, the bright square of sky shrinking above you, the dirt walls getting darker and cooler blue.
lines.camera: POV looking up at the shrinking sky, then a top-down shot of you going down
lines.gag: The sky shrinks to a stamp

lines.narration: And at the bottom, it's dark, it's quiet, and your thermometer says *sixty*.
lines.spoken: And at the bottom, it's dark, it's quiet, and your thermometer says... sixty.
lines.scene: The bottom of the hole is a little room: your mattress, a rug, the thermometer on its string reading 60; you breathe out, the sweat on your face drying.
lines.camera: Macro on the thermometer, rack to your relieved face
lines.gag: Your sweat drop shrinks away

lines.narration: You see, the ground is like a picnic *cooler*.
lines.scene: Mini-set: a picnic cooler in blazing sun on the grass, the lid sizzling; cross-section shows ice still solid at the bottom.
lines.camera: Dissolve to the cooler, slow push-in
lines.gag: An egg fries on the cooler lid while the ice inside sits frozen

lines.narration: The sun can bake the lid, but the heat takes *months* to reach the bottom.
lines.scene: Cross-section of your backyard: hot red ground at the top fading to cool blue at the bottom where you sit, a slow red wave crawling down only a little way.
lines.camera: Cross-section cut-away, tilt down from the lawn to you
lines.gag: The heat wave crawls down like it is stuck in syrup

lines.narration: For 40 days, Kyle partied, and you checked that string. Sixty. Every single *time*.
lines.spoken: For forty days, Kyle partied, and you checked that string. Sixty. Every single time.
lines.scene: Quick flash of you every 'day' at the hole, pulling up the string, nodding at the thermometer, while Kyle parties over the fence in the same sun.
lines.camera: Match cuts on the same framing, the shadows never moving
lines.gag: Same framing, same sun, same 60, a little taller pile of dirt each time

lines.narration: But your lid doesn't fit. A *sliver* of sun stabs right into your eyes.
lines.scene: You pulling a tinfoil-covered lid over the hole from below; it is a little too small, a blade of white sun cuts through the gap straight across your face.
lines.camera: Low angle up at the lid, the beam hits your eyes on 'sliver'
lines.gag: A laser-thin beam of sun right across your eyes

lines.narration: Then a *face* fills the gap.
lines.scene: Kyle's sunburnt face pressed into the gap in the lid, blocking the beam, eyes huge and bloodshot.
lines.camera: POV up at the gap
lines.gag: Kyle's face plugs the light

lines.narration: "Mole man... got *room*?"
lines.speaker: kyle
lines.scene: Kyle in the gap, sweaty and lobster-red, holding his half-deflated flamingo.
lines.camera: Hold on Kyle's face, slow push-in
lines.gag: The mocker begs

lines.narration: So Kyle does the smartest thing he's done in 40 days. He jams his giant *flamingo* into the gap.
lines.spoken: So Kyle does the smartest thing he's done in forty days. He jams his giant flamingo into the gap.
lines.scene: Kyle squeezing down the ladder, then stuffing the pink flamingo into the gap in the lid: its head and neck squash in, the light shrinks to nothing.
lines.camera: Low angle up, the flamingo's squashed face fills the gap on 'flamingo'
lines.gag: The flamingo's squashed face becomes your door

lines.narration: *Darkness*.
lines.scene: Black, then the faint glow of your phone screen lighting two faces on the mattress.
lines.camera: Hard cut to near-black, the phone glow fades up
lines.gag: Real dark for the first time in 40 days

lines.narration: It's 3 AM. And finally... it *feels* like it.
lines.spoken: It's three A.M. [sighs] And finally... it feels like it.
lines.scene: Close-up in the phone glow: the phone reads 3:00 AM; your eyes drooping into a happy sleepy smile, Kyle already snoring on your shoulder.
lines.camera: Mirror of the cold open: the phone sharp in the foreground, your face behind; the phone dims on the last word
lines.gag: Kyle snores on your shoulder
